summary: The two-phase authorization correctly handles cleanup winning: after acquiring the case lifecycle lock, an opener rereads the latest catalog chain under the catalog lock and must reject before DB open if cleanup has quarantined/tombstoned the case. The lock nesting order is acyclic if all paths follow case-before-catalog. A remaining TOCTOU gap is that the SDD does not explicitly require retaining the case lifecycle lock continuously across second authorization and OpenVerified/DB/sidecar/key opening, or retaining it through cleanup's handle closure/deletion/tombstone. The matrix tests only cleanup-wins, not opener-wins contention. Clarify lock lifetime and cover both orderings before approving the guarantee.

findings.title: Lifecycle-lock hold interval and opener-wins cleanup race are unspecified
findings.evidence: §3 step 3 releases the catalog lock after reauthorizing, then step 4 performs OpenVerified and opens DB/sidecar/key. Safety in this gap relies on the case lifecycle lock remaining held, but the SDD does not define its continuous hold/release boundary. Cleanup's durable quarantine and deletion likewise need mutual exclusion with active opens/handles. §6 currently specifies only the opener-waits/cleanup-wins branch.
findings.risk: If the case lock is released after reauthorization or only protects a short check, cleanup may alter/delete case files between authorization and open or during active use, invalidating the stale-state fencing guarantee.
findings.required_change: Specify that the same OS case lifecycle lock is continuously held from before the second catalog read through relevant verified opens and protected operations. Specify cleanup holds it through durable quarantine, closure of active handles, deletion, parent Sync, and tombstone; alternatively define an equivalent active-handle fencing mechanism. Add deterministic opener-wins contention coverage proving cleanup blocks until the protected scope ends, then cleanup completes and all later openers reject before DB open. Cover receipt/restart paths and bounded completion.
